newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says dispute over diplomats is India's affair.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says dispute over diplomats is India's affair.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said Thursday a flap with New Delhi involving two U.S. diplomats was India's "internal affair" and the diplomats had not been asked to leave the country, as some media reported.

"I don't really have much to give you on that, except to say that from what I understand this is an internal decision -- internal affair of the Indian government," spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters. "And you'll have to ask the Indian government about this, not us," he added.
"I'm not aware that anybody's been expelled from any country. We certainly hope that will not be the case...I'm not aware that anyone's been asked to leave anyplace," he said.
The Hindustan Times reported on Thursday that India would ask two U.S. diplomats to leave after an Indian intelligence official was accused of having unauthorised links with them.
The newspaper did not name the diplomats but said one was the local CIA station director.
In Washington, the Central Intelligence Agency said it would have no comment.
But U.S. officials told Reuters the two diplomats, who have not been identified, had not left India. They suggested the dispute had more to do with Indian domestic politics than substance.

The Hindustan Times said the decision to ask "the Americans to leave quietly" was made at a meeting of senior civil servants, including the chief of the home (interior) and foreign intelligence departments, and senior Home Ministry officials.
India's Foreign Ministry declined to comment on the report.
